content.content:
1	# Command Processor (CP) — Design
2	
3	**Scope:** the Vortex Command Processor control plane — the hardware
4	([`hw/rtl/cp/`](../../hw/rtl/cp/)), its functional twin used by the
5	simulators ([`sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp)),
6	and the async runtime that drives it
7	([`sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h)).
8	
9	Terminology used throughout this document:
10	
11	- **RTL CP** — the SystemVerilog hardware in `hw/rtl/cp/*.sv`.
12	- **Emulation CP** (a.k.a. **Simulation CP**) — the C++ model
13	  `sim/common/cmd_processor.{h,cpp}`, instantiated and ticked by the
14	  simx / rtlsim / gem5 backends.
15	
16	The CP is the single control plane through which the host submits work
17	to the GPU: memory transfers, DCR (device control register) programming,
18	kernel launch, fences, events, and cache maintenance. On FPGA targets
19	(XRT and OPAE) it is the **sole** launch/DCR path — the legacy AP_CTRL
20	launch FSM and per-AFU DCR machinery have been removed.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. Architecture overview
25	
26	```
27	   Host (runtime)                         Device
28	   ─────────────                          ──────
29	   vortex2.h enqueue                      ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
30	        │                                 │             VX_cp_core                 │
31	   per-queue worker thread                │                                        │
32	        │ build 64B command line          │  AXI-Lite ─► VX_cp_axil_regfile        │
33	        ▼                                 │   (doorbell: Q_TAIL_LO/HI)             │
34	   host-pinned ring  ◄───── AR ────────── │      │                                 │
35	   (host_mem_alloc)                       │      ▼  per queue                       │
36	        │  doorbell (MMIO)                │  VX_cp_fetch ─► VX_cp_unpack ─► VX_cp_engine
37	        ▼                                 │      │ (ring walker)        (FSM, bids) │
38	   CP_REG Q_TAIL ──────────────────────► │      ▼                                 │
39	                                          │  4× VX_cp_arbiter (KMU/DMA/DCR/EVENT)  │
40	   seqnum poll  ◄──── AW/W (cmpl_addr) ── │      │                                 │
41	   (Q_SEQNUM / completion writeback)      │  ┌───┴────┬─────────┬──────────┐      │
42	                                          │  ▼        ▼         ▼          ▼      │
43	                                          │ launch  dcr_proxy  dma       event_unit│
44	                                          │ (KMU)   (DCR bus)  (host/dev) (counters)│
45	                                          │      │        │        │         │     │
46	                                          │      └────────┴── VX_cp_completion ◄───┘
47	                                          │           (retire → seqnum writeback)  │
48	                                          └───────────────────────────────────────┘
49	```
50	
51	The CP is **N parallel command engines** (one per queue), feeding **four
52	round-robin arbiters** that serialize access to four shared resources:
53	the kernel-management unit (KMU launch), the DMA engine, the DCR bus, and
54	the event unit. The command ring lives in **host memory**; the CP fetches
55	from it over a dedicated AXI host port and writes completions back to host
56	memory over the same port.
57	
58	Implemented in [`VX_cp_core.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv); the engine
59	count, ring size, and AXI ID width come from `VX_config.toml`'s `[cp]`
60	block with safe defaults in
61	[`VX_cp_pkg.sv:31-50`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L31) (`NUM_QUEUES=1`,
62	`RING_SIZE_LOG2=16` → 64 KiB ring, `MAX_CMDS_PER_CL=5`, `AXI_TID_WIDTH=6`).
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 2. Command format
67	
68	A command is a header plus an opcode-specific payload, packed into 64-byte
69	cache lines (up to 5 commands per line; a zero header terminates the line).
70	The decoded record is `cmd_t` in
71	[`VX_cp_pkg.sv:97-103`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L97).
72	
73	**Header** (4 B, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:84-88`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L84)):
74	
75	```
76	{ reserved[15:0], flags[7:0], opcode[7:0] }
77	```
78	
79	Flags: `F_PROFILE` (bit 0) appends an 8 B profile-slot trailer;
80	`F_FENCE_PRE` (bit 1) ([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:81-82`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L81)).
81	
82	**Opcodes** ([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:63-75`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L63)) and
83	their on-wire sizes ([`cmd_size_bytes`, `VX_cp_pkg.sv:163-181`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L163)):
84	
85	| Opcode | Value | Size (B) | Purpose |
86	|---|---|---|---|
87	| `CMD_NOP` | 0x00 | 4 | Padding / ring alignment |
88	| `CMD_MEM_WRITE` | 0x01 | 28 | Host → device copy |
89	| `CMD_MEM_READ` | 0x02 | 28 | Device → host copy |
90	| `CMD_MEM_COPY` | 0x03 | 28 | Device → device copy |
91	| `CMD_DCR_WRITE` | 0x04 | 20 | Write a device control register |
92	| `CMD_DCR_READ` | 0x05 | 20 | Read a DCR (result in `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`) |
93	| `CMD_LAUNCH` | 0x06 | 12 | Pulse KMU start, wait for drain |
94	| `CMD_FENCE` | 0x07 | 8 | Ordering barrier (see §7) |
95	| `CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL` | 0x08 | 20 | Write a counter slot |
96	| `CMD_EVENT_WAIT` | 0x09 | 28 | Spin until counter satisfies compare |
97	| `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` | 0x0A | 12 | Per-core cache flush sweep |
98	| `CMD_DRAW` | 0x0C | 8 | Device-orchestrated graphics draw (Emulation CP only — RTL mirror deferred, §8.1) |
99	
100	`+8 B` to any size when `F_PROFILE` is set. `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` is an
101	addition beyond the original proposal command set (AMD `ACQUIRE_MEM`-style
102	maintenance). `CMD_DRAW` collapses the graphics front-end's whole launch+DCR
103	recipe into one command that the CP expands device-side (§8.1); it is
104	capability-gated (`SUPPORTS_DRAW`, §6) so a CP without it takes an equivalent
105	ring-batch fallback.
106	
107	`CMD_EVENT_WAIT` carries a compare op in `arg2[1:0]`
108	(`WAIT_OP_EQ/GE/GT/NE`, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:109-114`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L109)).
109	`CMD_FENCE` carries scope masks in `arg0[1:0]` (`FENCE_DMA_BIT`,
110	`FENCE_GPU_BIT`, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:120-121`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L120)).
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 3. RTL CP module inventory
115	
116	`hw/rtl/cp/` (~3500 LOC). Interfaces are split into separate `VX_cp_*_if.sv`
117	bundles per the project rule that `RTL_PKGS` carries only `*_pkg.sv`.
118	
119	| Module | Role |
120	|---|---|
121	| [`VX_cp_pkg.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv) | Opcodes, header/`cmd_t`/`cpe_state_t` structs, resource enum, `cmd_size_bytes`. |
122	| [`VX_cp_core.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv) | Top level: regfile, N×(fetch+engine), 4 arbiters, the 5 resource units, dual AXI xbars, `cp_busy`/`irq` aggregation. |
123	| [`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv) | The only AXI-Lite slave. Global regs + per-queue blocks; atomic doorbell commit; caps registers. |
124	| [`VX_cp_fetch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_fetch.sv) | Per-queue ring walker: ARs one 64 B cache line at `ring_base + (head & mask)`, single outstanding (no prefetch). |
125	| [`VX_cp_unpack.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_unpack.sv) | Per-offset single-command decoder (one command/cycle; refactored from a combinational whole-line walk for timing). |
126	| [`VX_cp_engine.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv) | Per-queue FSM `IDLE→DECODE→BID→WAIT_DONE→RETIRE`; classifies opcode→resource and retires via valid/ready handshake. |
127	| [`VX_cp_arbiter.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv) | Generic round-robin, instantiated 4× (one per resource). |
128	| [`VX_cp_launch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_launch.sv) | KMU start/busy wrapper: pulse start, hold grant until `busy` deasserts (drain). |
129	| [`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv) | DCR req/rsp gateway; also drives the per-core `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` sweep; publishes last read in `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`. |
130	| [`VX_cp_dma.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv) | Dual-port burst DMA (`axi_host` + `axi_dev`); opcode routes ports; ≤4 KB INCR chunks. |
131	| [`VX_cp_event_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv) | `EVENT_SIGNAL` write + `EVENT_WAIT` poll-spin against host/device counter slots. |
132	| [`VX_cp_completion.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv) | Per-source 1-deep latch + shared drain FIFO with `retire_ready` backpressure; AXI write of 8 B seqnum to `cmpl_addr`. |
133	| [`VX_cp_axi_xbar.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axi_xbar.sv) | N-source round-robin fan-in to one AXI master, TID-prefix response routing. |
134	| [`VX_cp_axi_to_membus.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axi_to_membus.sv) | AXI4 → `VX_mem_bus_if` bridge for the OPAE AFU's req/rsp fabric. |
135	| [`VX_cp_profiling.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_profiling.sv) | Free-running cycle counter (skeleton; see §10). |
136	| [`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv), interfaces `VX_cp_axi_m_if`, `VX_cp_axil_s_if`, `VX_cp_gpu_if`, `VX_cp_engine_bid_if` | AXI master / AXI-Lite slave / GPU DCR+start-busy / CPE-bid bundles. |
137	
138	Per-module Verilator unit tests live under `hw/unittest/cp_*`
139	(`cp_arbiter, cp_axil_regfile, cp_axi_path, cp_core, cp_dcr_proxy,
140	cp_dma, cp_engine, cp_launch, cp_unpack`).
141	
142	### 3.1 Dual AXI topology
143	
144	`VX_cp_core` builds **two** AXI crossbars
145	([`VX_cp_core.sv:386-431`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L386)):
146	
147	- **Host xbar** — fan-in of all fetch engines + completion + the DMA
148	  host port → one `axi_host` master that reaches host (pinned) memory.
149	- **Device xbar** — DMA device port + event unit → one `axi_dev` master
150	  that reaches device memory.
151	
152	`VX_cp_dma` routes its two ports by opcode
153	([`VX_cp_dma.sv:95-96`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L95)):
154	`MEM_WRITE` = host→dev, `MEM_READ` = dev→host, `MEM_COPY` = dev→dev.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 4. Per-queue engine and arbitration
159	
160	Each queue has a `cpe_state_t`
161	([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:130-141`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L130)): `ring_base`,
162	`ring_size_mask`, `head_addr`, `cmpl_addr`, `tail`, `head`, `seqnum`,
163	`prio`, `enabled`, `profile_en`.
164	
165	`VX_cp_engine` runs `IDLE→DECODE→BID→WAIT_DONE→RETIRE`
166	([`VX_cp_engine.sv:126-185`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L126)). It
167	classifies each opcode to one of `RES_KMU/RES_DMA/RES_DCR/RES_EVT`
168	([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:149-154`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L149)), raises a bid
169	to that resource's arbiter, waits for completion, then retires through
170	`VX_cp_completion` using a valid/ready handshake
171	([`VX_cp_engine.sv:173-181`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L173)) so no
172	seqnum is dropped when multiple engines retire in the same cycle. `NOP`
173	and `FENCE` retire immediately.
174	
175	The four arbiters are plain round-robin. `VX_cp_arbiter` exposes a
176	`bid_priority` input but it is currently **unused**
177	([`VX_cp_arbiter.sv:89-94`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv#L89)) — see §10.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 5. Register map (AXI-Lite)
182	
183	`VX_cp_axil_regfile` is the sole AXI-Lite slave
184	([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:12-44`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L12)):
185	
186	- **Globals** `0x000–0x024`: control, status, and read-only capability
187	  registers `GPU_DEV_CAPS` / `GPU_ISA_CAPS` (`0x018–0x024`), packed from
188	  config macros ([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:121-139`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L121)).
189	- **Per-queue block** at `0x100 + qid*0x40`: ring base/size, head/cmpl
190	  addresses, doorbell `Q_TAIL_LO/HI`, `Q_SEQNUM`, and `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`
191	  (`+0x30`, [`:205`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L205)).
192	
193	The doorbell commits atomically on the `Q_TAIL_HI` write
194	([`:333-336`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L333)); undecoded
195	addresses return DECERR.
196	
197	> **FPGA/sim divergence:** the RTL regfile has **no** `CP_SATP_LO/HI`
198	> registers. The Emulation CP *does* (`0x028/0x02C`,
199	> [`cmd_processor.cpp:75-76`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L75)) and
200	> the runtime always writes them
201	> ([`device.cpp:303-304`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L303)). See §8.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 6. Capability registers
206	
207	A single source of truth for device/ISA capabilities is exposed through
208	the CP and consumed identically by every backend (the
209	`caps_cp_consolidation` proposal, fully realized):
210	
211	- RTL: `GPU_DEV_CAPS` / `GPU_ISA_CAPS` RO regs
212	  ([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:121-139`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L121)).
213	- Emulation CP: same map
214	  ([`cmd_processor.cpp:30-49,126-129`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L30)).
215	- Runtime: one `decode_caps()` in
216	  [`sw/runtime/common/caps.h`](../../sw/runtime/common/caps.h), read over
217	  the CP regfile on every backend
218	  ([`device.cpp:275`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L275)).
219	
220	The duplicated capability blocks were removed from the XRT AFU shell.
221	(The OPAE AFU still carries some — see §10.)
222	
223	`GPU_DEV_CAPS` bit 25 **`SUPPORTS_DRAW`** advertises whether the CP expands
224	`CMD_DRAW` device-side (§8.1). The Emulation CP sets it (=1); the RTL CP clears
225	it (=0, mirror deferred), and the runtime consumes the bit in `cp_submit_draw`
226	([`queue.cpp`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp)): with the cap set it issues one
227	`CMD_DRAW`, otherwise it streams the byte-identical launch+DCR ring batch — so the
228	graphics driver calls `vx_enqueue_draw` unconditionally on every backend.
229	
230	---
231	
232	## 7. Resource units
233	
234	- **KMU launch** ([`VX_cp_launch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_launch.sv)) —
235	  `IDLE→PULSE_START→WAIT_BUSY→WAIT_DRAIN`; holds the KMU grant until
236	  `busy` falls, so a queue serializes its own launches.
237	- **DCR proxy** ([`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv)) —
238	  drives DCR write/read on the GPU's DCR bus and runs the per-core
239	  `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` sweep of `VX_DCR_BASE_CACHE_FLUSH`
240	  ([`:108-135`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv#L108)).
241	- **DMA** ([`VX_cp_dma.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv)) — dual-port
242	  multi-beat bursts in ≤4 KB INCR chunks
243	  ([`:81-178`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L81)).
244	- **Event unit** ([`VX_cp_event_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv)) —
245	  `EVENT_SIGNAL` writes a counter slot; `EVENT_WAIT` AR-polls until the
246	  compare passes ([`:124-129`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv#L124)).
247	- **Completion** ([`VX_cp_completion.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv)) —
248	  collects retirements (per-source latch + shared FIFO with `retire_ready`
249	  backpressure) and writes the 8 B seqnum to the queue's `cmpl_addr`
250	  ([`:60-208`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv#L60)).
251	
252	`irq` pulses on retire ([`VX_cp_core.sv:459-471`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L459))
253	but is not yet wired to a host ISR (§10).
254	
255	---
256	
257	## 8. Emulation / Simulation CP
258	
259	[`sim/common/cmd_processor.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp)
260	is a functional C++ twin (`vortex::CommandProcessor`): single-threaded,
261	one `tick()` per cycle, modelling a single queue (`q0_`). It is embedded
262	and ticked by the **simx, rtlsim, and gem5** backends inside their
263	`cp_reg_*` MMIO handlers (e.g.
264	[`sw/runtime/rtlsim/vortex.cpp:49,75-82`](../../sw/runtime/rtlsim/vortex.cpp#L49));
265	`host_mem_alloc` returns a `malloc` buffer whose pointer doubles as the
266	device-visible address.
267	
268	The Emulation CP's MMIO map matches the RTL regfile **plus**:
269	
270	- `CP_SATP_LO/HI` at `0x028/0x02C`
271	  ([`cmd_processor.cpp:75-76`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L75)),
272	- `CP_DEV_CAPS.VM_ENABLED` (bit 24,
273	  [`:117-122`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L117)),
274	- a software page-table walk `cp_translate` (Sv32/Sv39, megapage-aware,
275	  [`:157-201`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L157)) honoring the
276	  `MEM_FLAG_PHYSICAL` flag ([`:138,440-451`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L138)).
277	
278	This means **CP DMA is MMU-aware in simulation but not on FPGA** — a
279	deliberate phased rollout (runtime + emulation first, RTL walker later;
280	see §10).
281	
282	### 8.1 Device-orchestrated graphics draw (`CMD_DRAW` / `OP_DRAW`)
283	
284	The Emulation CP implements `CMD_DRAW` (0x0C) so a whole graphics draw is **one
285	command the CP expands device-side**, not a host-recorded sequence of launches +
286	DCR writes. `CMD_DRAW` points at a resident **draw descriptor** (`{u32 num_steps,
287	DrawStep steps[]}`, 28 B/step); the CP walks it with a `DrawStep/DrawLaunchWait`
288	FSM ([`cmd_processor.cpp:447-459,555-577`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L447)),
289	issuing each stage's DCR config + KMU launch and **draining each launch as the
290	inter-stage barrier** — the same drain-ordering the sort-middle front end
291	(expand→setup→bin→RASTER→FS→OM) needs, with no host round-trip mid-draw. The host
292	records the descriptor once and rings the doorbell once.
293	
294	The device side is shipped and validated on simx+rtlsim (`vx_enqueue_draw` →
295	`cp_submit_draw`, byte-identical to the multi-launch batch). The **RTL CP mirror is
296	deferred**: RTL CP clears `SUPPORTS_DRAW` (§6), so on the FPGA path the runtime
297	streams the equivalent launch+DCR ring batch. A future `OP_TRACE`/`OP_DISPATCH`
298	would extend the same mechanism to ray-tracing/compute so a mixed raster+RT frame
299	becomes one CP batch (tracked in the gfx_v2 master plan).
300	
301	---
302	
303	## 9. Runtime architecture
304	
305	The runtime ([`sw/runtime/`](../../sw/runtime/)) is built around a
306	**`callbacks_t` dlopen dispatcher** with a minimal 6-function transport
307	HAL ([`sw/runtime/common/callbacks.h:45-74`](../../sw/runtime/common/callbacks.h#L45)):
308	`dev_open/close`, `cp_reg_read/write`, `host_mem_alloc/free`. Everything
309	above that — command encoding, queues, events, buffers, VM — is
310	backend-agnostic common code. This is the design from the
311	`cp_pure_v2_callbacks` addendum; it superseded the compile-time
312	`vx::Platform` model of `cp_runtime_impl_proposal`.
313	
314	Layout:
315	
316	- [`include/vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h) — the async
317	  API; [`include/vortex.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex.h) — legacy
318	  API layered over it; helper headers `dxa.h`, `graphics.h`, `tensor.h`.
319	- [`common/`](../../sw/runtime/common/) — `device.cpp` (CP submit path),
320	  `queue.cpp` (per-queue worker threads + launch encoding), `event.cpp`,
321	  `buffer.cpp`, `module.cpp`, `vm.{h,cpp}`, `caps.h`, `callbacks.{h,inc}`,
322	  legacy wrappers, `vortex2_internal.h`.
323	- Backends: `simx/`, `rtlsim/`, `xrt/`, `opae/`, `gem5/`, and the `stub/`
324	  dispatcher.
325	
326	**Submit path:** `Device::cp_init()`
327	([`device.cpp:233`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L233)) programs each
328	queue's ring/head/cmpl addresses and sets `CP_REG_CTRL=0x1`. Each
329	`vx_enqueue_*` pushes a `Command` lambda onto a per-queue worker FIFO
330	([`queue.cpp:28,69`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L28)); the worker
331	waits on dependencies, encodes one 64 B cache line, memcpys it into the
332	host-pinned ring, rings the `Q_TAIL_LO/HI` doorbell, and busy-polls
333	`Q_SEQNUM` ([`device.cpp:334-398`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L334)).
334	A kernel launch is currently encoded as ~18 `CMD_DCR_WRITE`s to KMU DCRs
335	followed by `CMD_LAUNCH`, then `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` and a cout drain
336	([`queue.cpp:382-424`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L382)).
337	
338	> **vortex2.h vs the original "minimal" spec:** the shipped header is
339	> richer than the 34-function minimalist proposal — it keeps first-class
340	> `vx_module_h` and `vx_kernel_h` handles
341	> ([`vortex2.h:53-54`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h#L53)) plus
342	> rect-copy, fill-buffer, perf-dump, and max-occupancy helpers. This is
343	> the accepted current shape.
344	
345	### 9.1 FPGA backends
346	
347	- **XRT** ([`hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv)) —
348	  AXI-Lite is split on bit 12: `0x000–0x0FFF` → a minimal `VX_afu_ctrl`
349	  ap_ctrl stub + SCOPE; `0x1000–0x1FFF` → the CP regfile. The legacy
350	  launch FSM, DCR path, and dev-caps were **removed**; CP is the sole
351	  launch/DCR path (`vx_start = cp_gpu_if.start`,
352	  [`:342-353`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L342)). A dedicated
353	  `m_axi_host` port carries the ring
354	  ([`:305-316`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L305)); `axi_dev`
355	  joins memory bank 0 via `VX_axi_arb2`
356	  ([`:533-546`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L533)).
357	- **OPAE** ([`hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv)) —
358	  `VX_cp_core` instantiated at [`:328`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv#L328);
359	  `axi_host`→CCI-P and `axi_dev`→local memory both bridged through
360	  `VX_cp_axi_to_membus` ([`:372,530`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv#L372));
361	  MMIO word-address bit-10 demux (the 0x1000 byte boundary) to the CP
362	  regfile. The runtime
363	  ([`sw/runtime/opae/vortex.cpp`](../../sw/runtime/opae/vortex.cpp))
364	  implements `cp_reg_*` at `CP_BASE=0x1000` and `host_mem_alloc`.
365	
366	---
367	
368	## 10. Proposed but not yet implemented
369	
370	The following were specified across the source proposals (notably
371	`cp_v3_critical_review`) and remain **open**. They are recorded here so
372	the intent is not lost.
373	
374	**Correctness gaps (RTL ↔ emulation divergence):**
375	
376	1. **Byte-exact DMA in RTL.** `VX_cp_dma` rounds transfer size up to a
377	   64 B multiple (`rem_beats=(arg2+63)>>6`, `wstrb='1'`,
378	   [`VX_cp_dma.sv:119`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L119)) while the
379	   Emulation CP is byte-exact
380	   ([`cmd_processor.cpp:452-462`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L452)).
381	   Non-cache-line-aligned transfers can over-write on FPGA. Needs tail
382	   `wstrb` on the last beat (review item C-2/P-W4).
383	2. **VM in RTL.** Add `CP_SATP_LO/HI` regfile decode + a hardware
384	   page-table walker + TLB in `VX_cp_dma`, and route `F_MEM_PHYSICAL`, so
385	   FPGA matches the simulator's MMU-aware DMA (cp_pure_v2 VM Phase 2;
386	   review items P-W1/P-W3 and the SATP gap). Today VM works on
387	   simx/rtlsim/gem5 and silently no-ops on FPGA.
388	3. **Real `CMD_FENCE` semantics.** The engine retires FENCE as a NOP
389	   ([`VX_cp_engine.sv:109-112`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L109));
390	   it should honor `FENCE_DMA_BIT` / `FENCE_GPU_BIT` ordering (C-7).
391	4. **`dcr_req_ready` backpressure** in `VX_cp_dcr_proxy` — currently
392	   assumes the DCR bus always accepts
393	   ([`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv:118-125`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv#L118)) (C-3).
394	
395	**Performance / feature gaps:**
396	
397	5. **QMD-style atomic `CMD_LAUNCH`.** Replace the ~18-`CMD_DCR_WRITE`
398	   launch dance with grid/block/PC/args inline in the command
399	   ([`queue.cpp:382-414`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L382)). This
400	   is the precondition for true per-queue launch concurrency (A-1/E-3).
401	6. **Multi-queue everywhere.** RTL is parameterized on `NUM_QUEUES` but
402	   defaults to 1; the Emulation CP models only `q0_`; the runtime
403	   serializes launches. Real concurrency depends on item 5.
404	7. **EVENT_WAIT fairness + backoff.** `EVENT_WAIT` holds its arbiter
405	   grant for the whole wait
406	   ([`VX_cp_event_unit.sv:124-129`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv#L124));
407	   it should release between polls and back off (C-4).
408	8. **Priority arbitration.** Wire `VX_cp_arbiter.bid_priority` (currently
409	   unused, [`VX_cp_arbiter.sv:89-94`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv#L89))
410	   to the per-queue `prio` field.
411	9. **Profiling writeback.** `VX_cp_profiling` is a bare cycle counter;
412	   flesh it out to emit the 32 B `{queued,submit,start,end}` record, add a
413	   `CP_CYCLE_FREQ_HZ` register and the `0x040` MMIO block, so
414	   `vx_event_get_profiling` (already in the header) has hardware backing.
415	10. **Interrupt path.** Add IP_ISR/IER/GIER in the AFU and
416	    `xrt::ip::interrupt` so the runtime sleeps instead of busy-polling
417	    `Q_SEQNUM` (the `irq` pulse already exists,
418	    [`VX_cp_core.sv:459`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L459)).
419	11. **Host-coherent completion mailbox / `head_addr` writeback.** The CP
420	    tracks `head` internally and never DMAs it to `head_addr`; a cacheable
421	    host mailbox would avoid per-poll MMIO reads (E-10).
422	12. **`dcr_cp` 0x080–0x0BF DCR reservation** in `VX_types.toml` for
423	    future CP↔GPU coordination / multi-context KMU (never added).
424	13. **OPAE caps de-duplication.** The OPAE AFU still carries capability
425	    blocks that the XRT AFU has already delegated to the CP regfile.
426	
427	**Abandoned / superseded directions** (recorded so they are not
428	revived by accident): the device-memory ring + per-command DMA of the
429	original `command_processor_proposal` (replaced by the host-memory ring);
430	the `DEDICATED`/`SHARED` DMA build toggle (replaced by always-on dual
431	`axi_host`/`axi_dev`); the AP_CTRL legacy compat mode and `VORTEX_USE_CP`
432	opt-in (legacy path removed outright); the compile-time `vx::Platform`
433	runtime model and file-rename layout of `cp_runtime_impl_proposal`
434	(replaced by the `callbacks_t` HAL); and the "own runtime"
435	(LitePCIe/VFIO/Coyote) and extra per-card adapters (U250/U280/U55C/V80/
436	KV260) of `command_processor_redesign` — XRT and OPAE are the only live
437	hardware paths.
438	
439	---
440	
441	## 11. Source proposals
442	
443	This design consolidates and supersedes the following proposals
444	(now removed from `docs/proposals/`): `command_processor_proposal.md`,
445	`command_processor_redesign.md`, `caps_cp_consolidation_proposal.md`,
446	`cp_rtl_impl_proposal.md`, `cp_runtime_impl_proposal.md`,
447	`cp_v3_critical_review.md`, `cp_pure_v2_callbacks_proposal.md`,
448	`cp_xrt_integration_plan.md`, `cp_opae_integration_plan.md`.

# Command Processor (CP) — Design

**Scope:** the Vortex Command Processor control plane — the hardware
([`hw/rtl/cp/`](../../hw/rtl/cp/)), its functional twin used by the
simulators ([`sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp)),
and the async runtime that drives it
([`sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h)).

Terminology used throughout this document:

- **RTL CP** — the SystemVerilog hardware in `hw/rtl/cp/*.sv`.
- **Emulation CP** (a.k.a. **Simulation CP**) — the C++ model
  `sim/common/cmd_processor.{h,cpp}`, instantiated and ticked by the
  simx / rtlsim / gem5 backends.

The CP is the single control plane through which the host submits work
to the GPU: memory transfers, DCR (device control register) programming,
kernel launch, fences, events, and cache maintenance. On FPGA targets
(XRT and OPAE) it is the **sole** launch/DCR path — the legacy AP_CTRL
launch FSM and per-AFU DCR machinery have been removed.

---

## 1. Architecture overview

```
   Host (runtime)                         Device
   ─────────────                          ──────
   vortex2.h enqueue                      ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                                 │             VX_cp_core                 │
   per-queue worker thread                │                                        │
        │ build 64B command line          │  AXI-Lite ─► VX_cp_axil_regfile        │
        ▼                                 │   (doorbell: Q_TAIL_LO/HI)             │
   host-pinned ring  ◄───── AR ────────── │      │                                 │
   (host_mem_alloc)                       │      ▼  per queue                       │
        │  doorbell (MMIO)                │  VX_cp_fetch ─► VX_cp_unpack ─► VX_cp_engine
        ▼                                 │      │ (ring walker)        (FSM, bids) │
   CP_REG Q_TAIL ──────────────────────► │      ▼                                 │
                                          │  4× VX_cp_arbiter (KMU/DMA/DCR/EVENT)  │
   seqnum poll  ◄──── AW/W (cmpl_addr) ── │      │                                 │
   (Q_SEQNUM / completion writeback)      │  ┌───┴────┬─────────┬──────────┐      │
                                          │  ▼        ▼         ▼          ▼      │
                                          │ launch  dcr_proxy  dma       event_unit│
                                          │ (KMU)   (DCR bus)  (host/dev) (counters)│
                                          │      │        │        │         │     │
                                          │      └────────┴── VX_cp_completion ◄───┘
                                          │           (retire → seqnum writeback)  │
                                          └───────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The CP is **N parallel command engines** (one per queue), feeding **four
round-robin arbiters** that serialize access to four shared resources:
the kernel-management unit (KMU launch), the DMA engine, the DCR bus, and
the event unit. The command ring lives in **host memory**; the CP fetches
from it over a dedicated AXI host port and writes completions back to host
memory over the same port.

Implemented in [`VX_cp_core.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv); the engine
count, ring size, and AXI ID width come from `VX_config.toml`'s `[cp]`
block with safe defaults in
[`VX_cp_pkg.sv:31-50`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L31) (`NUM_QUEUES=1`,
`RING_SIZE_LOG2=16` → 64 KiB ring, `MAX_CMDS_PER_CL=5`, `AXI_TID_WIDTH=6`).

---

## 2. Command format

A command is a header plus an opcode-specific payload, packed into 64-byte
cache lines (up to 5 commands per line; a zero header terminates the line).
The decoded record is `cmd_t` in
[`VX_cp_pkg.sv:97-103`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L97).

**Header** (4 B, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:84-88`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L84)):

```
{ reserved[15:0], flags[7:0], opcode[7:0] }
```

Flags: `F_PROFILE` (bit 0) appends an 8 B profile-slot trailer;
`F_FENCE_PRE` (bit 1) ([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:81-82`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L81)).

**Opcodes** ([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:63-75`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L63)) and
their on-wire sizes ([`cmd_size_bytes`, `VX_cp_pkg.sv:163-181`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L163)):

| Opcode | Value | Size (B) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMD_NOP` | 0x00 | 4 | Padding / ring alignment |
| `CMD_MEM_WRITE` | 0x01 | 28 | Host → device copy |
| `CMD_MEM_READ` | 0x02 | 28 | Device → host copy |
| `CMD_MEM_COPY` | 0x03 | 28 | Device → device copy |
| `CMD_DCR_WRITE` | 0x04 | 20 | Write a device control register |
| `CMD_DCR_READ` | 0x05 | 20 | Read a DCR (result in `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`) |
| `CMD_LAUNCH` | 0x06 | 12 | Pulse KMU start, wait for drain |
| `CMD_FENCE` | 0x07 | 8 | Ordering barrier (see §7) |
| `CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL` | 0x08 | 20 | Write a counter slot |
| `CMD_EVENT_WAIT` | 0x09 | 28 | Spin until counter satisfies compare |
| `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` | 0x0A | 12 | Per-core cache flush sweep |
| `CMD_DRAW` | 0x0C | 8 | Device-orchestrated graphics draw (Emulation CP only — RTL mirror deferred, §8.1) |

`+8 B` to any size when `F_PROFILE` is set. `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` is an
addition beyond the original proposal command set (AMD `ACQUIRE_MEM`-style
maintenance). `CMD_DRAW` collapses the graphics front-end's whole launch+DCR
recipe into one command that the CP expands device-side (§8.1); it is
capability-gated (`SUPPORTS_DRAW`, §6) so a CP without it takes an equivalent
ring-batch fallback.

`CMD_EVENT_WAIT` carries a compare op in `arg2[1:0]`
(`WAIT_OP_EQ/GE/GT/NE`, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:109-114`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L109)).
`CMD_FENCE` carries scope masks in `arg0[1:0]` (`FENCE_DMA_BIT`,
`FENCE_GPU_BIT`, [`VX_cp_pkg.sv:120-121`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L120)).

---

## 3. RTL CP module inventory

`hw/rtl/cp/` (~3500 LOC). Interfaces are split into separate `VX_cp_*_if.sv`
bundles per the project rule that `RTL_PKGS` carries only `*_pkg.sv`.

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| [`VX_cp_pkg.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv) | Opcodes, header/`cmd_t`/`cpe_state_t` structs, resource enum, `cmd_size_bytes`. |
| [`VX_cp_core.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv) | Top level: regfile, N×(fetch+engine), 4 arbiters, the 5 resource units, dual AXI xbars, `cp_busy`/`irq` aggregation. |
| [`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv) | The only AXI-Lite slave. Global regs + per-queue blocks; atomic doorbell commit; caps registers. |
| [`VX_cp_fetch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_fetch.sv) | Per-queue ring walker: ARs one 64 B cache line at `ring_base + (head & mask)`, single outstanding (no prefetch). |
| [`VX_cp_unpack.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_unpack.sv) | Per-offset single-command decoder (one command/cycle; refactored from a combinational whole-line walk for timing). |
| [`VX_cp_engine.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv) | Per-queue FSM `IDLE→DECODE→BID→WAIT_DONE→RETIRE`; classifies opcode→resource and retires via valid/ready handshake. |
| [`VX_cp_arbiter.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv) | Generic round-robin, instantiated 4× (one per resource). |
| [`VX_cp_launch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_launch.sv) | KMU start/busy wrapper: pulse start, hold grant until `busy` deasserts (drain). |
| [`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv) | DCR req/rsp gateway; also drives the per-core `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` sweep; publishes last read in `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`. |
| [`VX_cp_dma.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv) | Dual-port burst DMA (`axi_host` + `axi_dev`); opcode routes ports; ≤4 KB INCR chunks. |
| [`VX_cp_event_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv) | `EVENT_SIGNAL` write + `EVENT_WAIT` poll-spin against host/device counter slots. |
| [`VX_cp_completion.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv) | Per-source 1-deep latch + shared drain FIFO with `retire_ready` backpressure; AXI write of 8 B seqnum to `cmpl_addr`. |
| [`VX_cp_axi_xbar.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axi_xbar.sv) | N-source round-robin fan-in to one AXI master, TID-prefix response routing. |
| [`VX_cp_axi_to_membus.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axi_to_membus.sv) | AXI4 → `VX_mem_bus_if` bridge for the OPAE AFU's req/rsp fabric. |
| [`VX_cp_profiling.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_profiling.sv) | Free-running cycle counter (skeleton; see §10). |
| [`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv), interfaces `VX_cp_axi_m_if`, `VX_cp_axil_s_if`, `VX_cp_gpu_if`, `VX_cp_engine_bid_if` | AXI master / AXI-Lite slave / GPU DCR+start-busy / CPE-bid bundles. |

Per-module Verilator unit tests live under `hw/unittest/cp_*`
(`cp_arbiter, cp_axil_regfile, cp_axi_path, cp_core, cp_dcr_proxy,
cp_dma, cp_engine, cp_launch, cp_unpack`).

### 3.1 Dual AXI topology

`VX_cp_core` builds **two** AXI crossbars
([`VX_cp_core.sv:386-431`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L386)):

- **Host xbar** — fan-in of all fetch engines + completion + the DMA
  host port → one `axi_host` master that reaches host (pinned) memory.
- **Device xbar** — DMA device port + event unit → one `axi_dev` master
  that reaches device memory.

`VX_cp_dma` routes its two ports by opcode
([`VX_cp_dma.sv:95-96`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L95)):
`MEM_WRITE` = host→dev, `MEM_READ` = dev→host, `MEM_COPY` = dev→dev.

---

## 4. Per-queue engine and arbitration

Each queue has a `cpe_state_t`
([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:130-141`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L130)): `ring_base`,
`ring_size_mask`, `head_addr`, `cmpl_addr`, `tail`, `head`, `seqnum`,
`prio`, `enabled`, `profile_en`.

`VX_cp_engine` runs `IDLE→DECODE→BID→WAIT_DONE→RETIRE`
([`VX_cp_engine.sv:126-185`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L126)). It
classifies each opcode to one of `RES_KMU/RES_DMA/RES_DCR/RES_EVT`
([`VX_cp_pkg.sv:149-154`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L149)), raises a bid
to that resource's arbiter, waits for completion, then retires through
`VX_cp_completion` using a valid/ready handshake
([`VX_cp_engine.sv:173-181`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L173)) so no
seqnum is dropped when multiple engines retire in the same cycle. `NOP`
and `FENCE` retire immediately.

The four arbiters are plain round-robin. `VX_cp_arbiter` exposes a
`bid_priority` input but it is currently **unused**
([`VX_cp_arbiter.sv:89-94`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv#L89)) — see §10.

---

## 5. Register map (AXI-Lite)

`VX_cp_axil_regfile` is the sole AXI-Lite slave
([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:12-44`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L12)):

- **Globals** `0x000–0x024`: control, status, and read-only capability
  registers `GPU_DEV_CAPS` / `GPU_ISA_CAPS` (`0x018–0x024`), packed from
  config macros ([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:121-139`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L121)).
- **Per-queue block** at `0x100 + qid*0x40`: ring base/size, head/cmpl
  addresses, doorbell `Q_TAIL_LO/HI`, `Q_SEQNUM`, and `Q_LAST_DCR_RSP`
  (`+0x30`, [`:205`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L205)).

The doorbell commits atomically on the `Q_TAIL_HI` write
([`:333-336`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L333)); undecoded
addresses return DECERR.

> **FPGA/sim divergence:** the RTL regfile has **no** `CP_SATP_LO/HI`
> registers. The Emulation CP *does* (`0x028/0x02C`,
> [`cmd_processor.cpp:75-76`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L75)) and
> the runtime always writes them
> ([`device.cpp:303-304`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L303)). See §8.

---

## 6. Capability registers

A single source of truth for device/ISA capabilities is exposed through
the CP and consumed identically by every backend (the
`caps_cp_consolidation` proposal, fully realized):

- RTL: `GPU_DEV_CAPS` / `GPU_ISA_CAPS` RO regs
  ([`VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv:121-139`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_axil_regfile.sv#L121)).
- Emulation CP: same map
  ([`cmd_processor.cpp:30-49,126-129`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L30)).
- Runtime: one `decode_caps()` in
  [`sw/runtime/common/caps.h`](../../sw/runtime/common/caps.h), read over
  the CP regfile on every backend
  ([`device.cpp:275`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L275)).

The duplicated capability blocks were removed from the XRT AFU shell.
(The OPAE AFU still carries some — see §10.)

`GPU_DEV_CAPS` bit 25 **`SUPPORTS_DRAW`** advertises whether the CP expands
`CMD_DRAW` device-side (§8.1). The Emulation CP sets it (=1); the RTL CP clears
it (=0, mirror deferred), and the runtime consumes the bit in `cp_submit_draw`
([`queue.cpp`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp)): with the cap set it issues one
`CMD_DRAW`, otherwise it streams the byte-identical launch+DCR ring batch — so the
graphics driver calls `vx_enqueue_draw` unconditionally on every backend.

---

## 7. Resource units

- **KMU launch** ([`VX_cp_launch.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_launch.sv)) —
  `IDLE→PULSE_START→WAIT_BUSY→WAIT_DRAIN`; holds the KMU grant until
  `busy` falls, so a queue serializes its own launches.
- **DCR proxy** ([`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv)) —
  drives DCR write/read on the GPU's DCR bus and runs the per-core
  `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` sweep of `VX_DCR_BASE_CACHE_FLUSH`
  ([`:108-135`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv#L108)).
- **DMA** ([`VX_cp_dma.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv)) — dual-port
  multi-beat bursts in ≤4 KB INCR chunks
  ([`:81-178`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L81)).
- **Event unit** ([`VX_cp_event_unit.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv)) —
  `EVENT_SIGNAL` writes a counter slot; `EVENT_WAIT` AR-polls until the
  compare passes ([`:124-129`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv#L124)).
- **Completion** ([`VX_cp_completion.sv`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv)) —
  collects retirements (per-source latch + shared FIFO with `retire_ready`
  backpressure) and writes the 8 B seqnum to the queue's `cmpl_addr`
  ([`:60-208`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_completion.sv#L60)).

`irq` pulses on retire ([`VX_cp_core.sv:459-471`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L459))
but is not yet wired to a host ISR (§10).

---

## 8. Emulation / Simulation CP

[`sim/common/cmd_processor.{h,cpp}`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp)
is a functional C++ twin (`vortex::CommandProcessor`): single-threaded,
one `tick()` per cycle, modelling a single queue (`q0_`). It is embedded
and ticked by the **simx, rtlsim, and gem5** backends inside their
`cp_reg_*` MMIO handlers (e.g.
[`sw/runtime/rtlsim/vortex.cpp:49,75-82`](../../sw/runtime/rtlsim/vortex.cpp#L49));
`host_mem_alloc` returns a `malloc` buffer whose pointer doubles as the
device-visible address.

The Emulation CP's MMIO map matches the RTL regfile **plus**:

- `CP_SATP_LO/HI` at `0x028/0x02C`
  ([`cmd_processor.cpp:75-76`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L75)),
- `CP_DEV_CAPS.VM_ENABLED` (bit 24,
  [`:117-122`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L117)),
- a software page-table walk `cp_translate` (Sv32/Sv39, megapage-aware,
  [`:157-201`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L157)) honoring the
  `MEM_FLAG_PHYSICAL` flag ([`:138,440-451`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L138)).

This means **CP DMA is MMU-aware in simulation but not on FPGA** — a
deliberate phased rollout (runtime + emulation first, RTL walker later;
see §10).

### 8.1 Device-orchestrated graphics draw (`CMD_DRAW` / `OP_DRAW`)

The Emulation CP implements `CMD_DRAW` (0x0C) so a whole graphics draw is **one
command the CP expands device-side**, not a host-recorded sequence of launches +
DCR writes. `CMD_DRAW` points at a resident **draw descriptor** (`{u32 num_steps,
DrawStep steps[]}`, 28 B/step); the CP walks it with a `DrawStep/DrawLaunchWait`
FSM ([`cmd_processor.cpp:447-459,555-577`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L447)),
issuing each stage's DCR config + KMU launch and **draining each launch as the
inter-stage barrier** — the same drain-ordering the sort-middle front end
(expand→setup→bin→RASTER→FS→OM) needs, with no host round-trip mid-draw. The host
records the descriptor once and rings the doorbell once.

The device side is shipped and validated on simx+rtlsim (`vx_enqueue_draw` →
`cp_submit_draw`, byte-identical to the multi-launch batch). The **RTL CP mirror is
deferred**: RTL CP clears `SUPPORTS_DRAW` (§6), so on the FPGA path the runtime
streams the equivalent launch+DCR ring batch. A future `OP_TRACE`/`OP_DISPATCH`
would extend the same mechanism to ray-tracing/compute so a mixed raster+RT frame
becomes one CP batch (tracked in the gfx_v2 master plan).

---

## 9. Runtime architecture

The runtime ([`sw/runtime/`](../../sw/runtime/)) is built around a
**`callbacks_t` dlopen dispatcher** with a minimal 6-function transport
HAL ([`sw/runtime/common/callbacks.h:45-74`](../../sw/runtime/common/callbacks.h#L45)):
`dev_open/close`, `cp_reg_read/write`, `host_mem_alloc/free`. Everything
above that — command encoding, queues, events, buffers, VM — is
backend-agnostic common code. This is the design from the
`cp_pure_v2_callbacks` addendum; it superseded the compile-time
`vx::Platform` model of `cp_runtime_impl_proposal`.

Layout:

- [`include/vortex2.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h) — the async
  API; [`include/vortex.h`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex.h) — legacy
  API layered over it; helper headers `dxa.h`, `graphics.h`, `tensor.h`.
- [`common/`](../../sw/runtime/common/) — `device.cpp` (CP submit path),
  `queue.cpp` (per-queue worker threads + launch encoding), `event.cpp`,
  `buffer.cpp`, `module.cpp`, `vm.{h,cpp}`, `caps.h`, `callbacks.{h,inc}`,
  legacy wrappers, `vortex2_internal.h`.
- Backends: `simx/`, `rtlsim/`, `xrt/`, `opae/`, `gem5/`, and the `stub/`
  dispatcher.

**Submit path:** `Device::cp_init()`
([`device.cpp:233`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L233)) programs each
queue's ring/head/cmpl addresses and sets `CP_REG_CTRL=0x1`. Each
`vx_enqueue_*` pushes a `Command` lambda onto a per-queue worker FIFO
([`queue.cpp:28,69`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L28)); the worker
waits on dependencies, encodes one 64 B cache line, memcpys it into the
host-pinned ring, rings the `Q_TAIL_LO/HI` doorbell, and busy-polls
`Q_SEQNUM` ([`device.cpp:334-398`](../../sw/runtime/common/device.cpp#L334)).
A kernel launch is currently encoded as ~18 `CMD_DCR_WRITE`s to KMU DCRs
followed by `CMD_LAUNCH`, then `CMD_CACHE_FLUSH` and a cout drain
([`queue.cpp:382-424`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L382)).

> **vortex2.h vs the original "minimal" spec:** the shipped header is
> richer than the 34-function minimalist proposal — it keeps first-class
> `vx_module_h` and `vx_kernel_h` handles
> ([`vortex2.h:53-54`](../../sw/runtime/include/vortex2.h#L53)) plus
> rect-copy, fill-buffer, perf-dump, and max-occupancy helpers. This is
> the accepted current shape.

### 9.1 FPGA backends

- **XRT** ([`hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv)) —
  AXI-Lite is split on bit 12: `0x000–0x0FFF` → a minimal `VX_afu_ctrl`
  ap_ctrl stub + SCOPE; `0x1000–0x1FFF` → the CP regfile. The legacy
  launch FSM, DCR path, and dev-caps were **removed**; CP is the sole
  launch/DCR path (`vx_start = cp_gpu_if.start`,
  [`:342-353`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L342)). A dedicated
  `m_axi_host` port carries the ring
  ([`:305-316`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L305)); `axi_dev`
  joins memory bank 0 via `VX_axi_arb2`
  ([`:533-546`](../../hw/rtl/afu/xrt/VX_afu_wrap.sv#L533)).
- **OPAE** ([`hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv)) —
  `VX_cp_core` instantiated at [`:328`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv#L328);
  `axi_host`→CCI-P and `axi_dev`→local memory both bridged through
  `VX_cp_axi_to_membus` ([`:372,530`](../../hw/rtl/afu/opae/vortex_afu.sv#L372));
  MMIO word-address bit-10 demux (the 0x1000 byte boundary) to the CP
  regfile. The runtime
  ([`sw/runtime/opae/vortex.cpp`](../../sw/runtime/opae/vortex.cpp))
  implements `cp_reg_*` at `CP_BASE=0x1000` and `host_mem_alloc`.

---

## 10. Proposed but not yet implemented

The following were specified across the source proposals (notably
`cp_v3_critical_review`) and remain **open**. They are recorded here so
the intent is not lost.

**Correctness gaps (RTL ↔ emulation divergence):**

1. **Byte-exact DMA in RTL.** `VX_cp_dma` rounds transfer size up to a
   64 B multiple (`rem_beats=(arg2+63)>>6`, `wstrb='1'`,
   [`VX_cp_dma.sv:119`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dma.sv#L119)) while the
   Emulation CP is byte-exact
   ([`cmd_processor.cpp:452-462`](../../sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp#L452)).
   Non-cache-line-aligned transfers can over-write on FPGA. Needs tail
   `wstrb` on the last beat (review item C-2/P-W4).
2. **VM in RTL.** Add `CP_SATP_LO/HI` regfile decode + a hardware
   page-table walker + TLB in `VX_cp_dma`, and route `F_MEM_PHYSICAL`, so
   FPGA matches the simulator's MMU-aware DMA (cp_pure_v2 VM Phase 2;
   review items P-W1/P-W3 and the SATP gap). Today VM works on
   simx/rtlsim/gem5 and silently no-ops on FPGA.
3. **Real `CMD_FENCE` semantics.** The engine retires FENCE as a NOP
   ([`VX_cp_engine.sv:109-112`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_engine.sv#L109));
   it should honor `FENCE_DMA_BIT` / `FENCE_GPU_BIT` ordering (C-7).
4. **`dcr_req_ready` backpressure** in `VX_cp_dcr_proxy` — currently
   assumes the DCR bus always accepts
   ([`VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv:118-125`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_dcr_proxy.sv#L118)) (C-3).

**Performance / feature gaps:**

5. **QMD-style atomic `CMD_LAUNCH`.** Replace the ~18-`CMD_DCR_WRITE`
   launch dance with grid/block/PC/args inline in the command
   ([`queue.cpp:382-414`](../../sw/runtime/common/queue.cpp#L382)). This
   is the precondition for true per-queue launch concurrency (A-1/E-3).
6. **Multi-queue everywhere.** RTL is parameterized on `NUM_QUEUES` but
   defaults to 1; the Emulation CP models only `q0_`; the runtime
   serializes launches. Real concurrency depends on item 5.
7. **EVENT_WAIT fairness + backoff.** `EVENT_WAIT` holds its arbiter
   grant for the whole wait
   ([`VX_cp_event_unit.sv:124-129`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_event_unit.sv#L124));
   it should release between polls and back off (C-4).
8. **Priority arbitration.** Wire `VX_cp_arbiter.bid_priority` (currently
   unused, [`VX_cp_arbiter.sv:89-94`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_arbiter.sv#L89))
   to the per-queue `prio` field.
9. **Profiling writeback.** `VX_cp_profiling` is a bare cycle counter;
   flesh it out to emit the 32 B `{queued,submit,start,end}` record, add a
   `CP_CYCLE_FREQ_HZ` register and the `0x040` MMIO block, so
   `vx_event_get_profiling` (already in the header) has hardware backing.
10. **Interrupt path.** Add IP_ISR/IER/GIER in the AFU and
    `xrt::ip::interrupt` so the runtime sleeps instead of busy-polling
    `Q_SEQNUM` (the `irq` pulse already exists,
    [`VX_cp_core.sv:459`](../../hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L459)).
11. **Host-coherent completion mailbox / `head_addr` writeback.** The CP
    tracks `head` internally and never DMAs it to `head_addr`; a cacheable
    host mailbox would avoid per-poll MMIO reads (E-10).
12. **`dcr_cp` 0x080–0x0BF DCR reservation** in `VX_types.toml` for
    future CP↔GPU coordination / multi-context KMU (never added).
13. **OPAE caps de-duplication.** The OPAE AFU still carries capability
    blocks that the XRT AFU has already delegated to the CP regfile.

**Abandoned / superseded directions** (recorded so they are not
revived by accident): the device-memory ring + per-command DMA of the
original `command_processor_proposal` (replaced by the host-memory ring);
the `DEDICATED`/`SHARED` DMA build toggle (replaced by always-on dual
`axi_host`/`axi_dev`); the AP_CTRL legacy compat mode and `VORTEX_USE_CP`
opt-in (legacy path removed outright); the compile-time `vx::Platform`
runtime model and file-rename layout of `cp_runtime_impl_proposal`
(replaced by the `callbacks_t` HAL); and the "own runtime"
(LitePCIe/VFIO/Coyote) and extra per-card adapters (U250/U280/U55C/V80/
KV260) of `command_processor_redesign` — XRT and OPAE are the only live
hardware paths.

---

## 11. Source proposals

This design consolidates and supersedes the following proposals
(now removed from `docs/proposals/`): `command_processor_proposal.md`,
`command_processor_redesign.md`, `caps_cp_consolidation_proposal.md`,
`cp_rtl_impl_proposal.md`, `cp_runtime_impl_proposal.md`,
`cp_v3_critical_review.md`, `cp_pure_v2_callbacks_proposal.md`,
`cp_xrt_integration_plan.md`, `cp_opae_integration_plan.md`.

6	// ============================================================================
7	// VX_cp_launch — KMU start/busy wrapper. Owned by the KMU resource arbiter.
8	//
9	// KMU arbitration holds for the entire duration of a launch:
10	//   IDLE         : no grant yet
11	//   PULSE_START  : grant just observed; assert `start` for one cycle
12	//   WAIT_BUSY    : Vortex pulls `busy` high (kernel started)
13	//   WAIT_DRAIN   : Vortex drops `busy` low (kernel done) → fire `done`,
14	//                  go back to IDLE
15	//
16	// The CPE that won the KMU arbiter holds its bid across all of these
17	// states; `done` releasing the bid lets the next CPE take its turn.
18	//
19	// `grant` is the OR of per-CPE grants from the KMU arbiter (the CP core
20	// glues all N bids onto this single input).
21	// ============================================================================
22	
23	module VX_cp_launch (
24	  input  wire  clk,
25	  input  wire  reset,
26	
27	  input  wire  grant,         // OR of per-CPE grants from KMU arbiter
28	  output logic start,         // pulsed to gpu_if.start (Vortex)
29	  input  wire  gpu_busy,      // from gpu_if.busy (Vortex)
30	  output logic done           // back to engine: launch fully drained
31	);
32	
33	  typedef enum logic [1:0] {
34	    S_IDLE,
35	    S_PULSE_START,
36	    S_WAIT_BUSY,
37	    S_WAIT_DRAIN
38	  } state_e;
39	
40	  state_e state;
41	
42	  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
43	    if (reset) begin
44	      state <= S_IDLE;
45	    end else begin
46	      case (state)
47	        S_IDLE: begin
48	          if (grant) state <= S_PULSE_START;
49	        end
50	        S_PULSE_START: begin
51	          state <= S_WAIT_BUSY;
52	        end
53	        S_WAIT_BUSY: begin
54	          // Vortex's busy might rise the next cycle after `start` fires;
55	          // we wait for that rising edge.
56	          if (gpu_busy) state <= S_WAIT_DRAIN;
57	        end
58	        S_WAIT_DRAIN: begin
59	          if (!gpu_busy) state <= S_IDLE;
60	        end
61	        default: state <= S_IDLE;
62	      endcase
63	    end
64	  end
65	
66	  always_comb begin
67	    start = (state == S_PULSE_START);
68	    done  = (state == S_WAIT_DRAIN) && !gpu_busy;
69	  end
70	
71	endmodule : VX_cp_launch

110	    WAIT_OP_EQ = 2'd0,
111	    WAIT_OP_GE = 2'd1,
112	    WAIT_OP_GT = 2'd2,
113	    WAIT_OP_NE = 2'd3
114	  } wait_op_e;
115	
116	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
117	  // FENCE op masks (encoded in arg0[1:0]).
118	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	  localparam int FENCE_DMA_BIT = 0;
121	  localparam int FENCE_GPU_BIT = 1;
122	
123	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
124	  // Per-CPE persistent state.
125	  //
126	  // One instance lives inside each VX_cp_engine. Host-visible registers in
127	  // the AXI-Lite slave write to these.
128	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
129	
130	  typedef struct packed {
131	    logic [63:0]                       ring_base;        // host IO addr of ring
132	    logic [VX_CP_RING_SIZE_LOG2_C-1:0] ring_size_mask;   // size_bytes - 1
133	    logic [63:0]                       head_addr;        // CP publishes head here
134	    logic [63:0]                       cmpl_addr;        // CP publishes seqnum here
135	    logic [63:0]                       tail;             // last committed via doorbell
136	    logic [63:0]                       head;             // CPE consumer pointer
137	    logic [63:0]                       seqnum;           // next-to-retire seqnum
138	    logic [1:0]                        prio;             // 0=lo, 3=hi
139	    logic                              enabled;
140	    logic                              profile_en;
141	  } cpe_state_t;
142	
143	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	  // Per-resource arbiter request (CPE -> arbiter).
145	  //
146	  // Each CPE has three such bid lines (KMU, DMA, DCR).
147	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
148	
149	  typedef enum logic [1:0] {
150	    RES_KMU = 2'd0,
151	    RES_DMA = 2'd1,
152	    RES_DCR = 2'd2,
153	    RES_EVT = 2'd3      // handles CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL + CMD_EVENT_WAIT
154	  } cp_resource_e;
155	
156	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
157	  // Helpers
158	  // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
159	
160	  // True for opcodes this CP decodes. VX_cp_unpack drops the rest of a
161	  // cache line on an unknown opcode: its size is unknowable, so walking on
162	  // would re-parse its payload bytes as phantom commands.
163	  function automatic logic cmd_opcode_valid(cp_opcode_e op);
164	    case (op)
165	      CMD_NOP,
166	      CMD_MEM_WRITE,
167	      CMD_MEM_READ,
168	      CMD_MEM_COPY,
169	      CMD_DCR_WRITE,
170	      CMD_DCR_READ,
171	      CMD_LAUNCH,
172	      CMD_FENCE,
173	      CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL,
174	      CMD_EVENT_WAIT,
175	      CMD_CACHE_FLUSH: return 1'b1;
176	      default:         return 1'b0;
177	    endcase
178	  endfunction
179	
180	  // Returns the on-wire byte size of a command given its opcode and the
181	  // F_PROFILE flag. Used by VX_cp_unpack to know how much of the cache
182	  // line to consume per command.
183	  function automatic int unsigned cmd_size_bytes(cp_opcode_e op,
184	                                                 logic profiled);
185	    int unsigned base;
186	    case (op)
187	      CMD_NOP:          base = 4;
188	      CMD_LAUNCH:       base = 12;
189	      CMD_FENCE:        base = 8;
190	      CMD_CACHE_FLUSH:  base = 12;
191	      CMD_DCR_WRITE:    base = 20;
192	      CMD_DCR_READ:     base = 20;
193	      CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL: base = 20;
194	      CMD_EVENT_WAIT:   base = 28;
195	      CMD_MEM_WRITE:    base = 28;
196	      CMD_MEM_READ:     base = 28;
197	      CMD_MEM_COPY:     base = 28;
198	      default:          base = 4;
199	    endcase
200	    return base + (profiled ? 8 : 0);
201	  endfunction

15	// cmd_processor.h — functional C++ model of the Command Processor.
16	// Shared by simx and rtlsim; presents the same cp_mmio_* MMIO surface to
17	// the runtime.
18	//
19	// Implements a `tick()`-per-cycle state machine that reads commands from a
20	// host-pinned ring in DRAM, dispatches them to the right resource (DCR proxy,
21	// launch, DMA), and publishes the retired sequence number back to a
22	// host-pinned completion slot.
23	//
24	// Address map (CP-internal, 0-based):
25	//   Globals (CP-internal offsets 0x000..0x0FF)
26	//     0x000 CP_CTRL       bit0=enable_global, bit1=reset_all
27	//     0x004 CP_STATUS     bit0=busy, bit1=error
28	//     0x008 CP_DEV_CAPS   {AXI_TID_W:8 | RING_LOG2:8 | NUM_QUEUES:8}
29	//     0x010 CP_CYCLE_LO
30	//     0x014 CP_CYCLE_HI
31	//     0x018 GPU_DEV_CAPS_LO  device-config caps, low 32 bits   (RO)
32	//     0x01C GPU_DEV_CAPS_HI  device-config caps, high 32 bits  (RO)
33	//     0x020 GPU_ISA_CAPS_LO  ISA caps, low 32 bits             (RO)
34	//     0x024 GPU_ISA_CAPS_HI  ISA caps, high 32 bits            (RO)
35	//   Per queue 0 (CP-internal offsets 0x100..0x13F)
36	//     0x100/04 Q_RING_BASE_LO/HI
37	//     0x108/0C Q_HEAD_ADDR_LO/HI   (where the CP publishes head)
38	//     0x110/14 Q_CMPL_ADDR_LO/HI   (where the CP publishes seqnum)
39	//     0x118    Q_RING_SIZE_LOG2
40	//     0x11C    Q_CONTROL          bit0=enable, bit1=reset
41	//     0x120    Q_TAIL_LO          (staging)
42	//     0x124    Q_TAIL_HI          (atomic commit)
43	//     0x128    Q_SEQNUM           (RO mirror)
44	//     0x12C    Q_ERROR
45	//     0x130    Q_LAST_DCR_RSP     (RO — latest CMD_DCR_READ response)
46	//
47	// CMD_DRAW (OP_DRAW, opcode 0x0C) — device-orchestrated draw.
48	//   A single ring command whose arg0 points at a resident *draw descriptor*:
49	//     uint32_t num_steps;                       // at offset 0
50	//     cmd_step  steps[num_steps];               // at offset 4, 28 B stride
51	//   Each step is a 28-byte cmd record (same byte layout decode_cmd reads):
52	//   {opcode:u8, flags:u8, reserved:u16, arg0:u64, arg1:u64, arg2:u64}. The CP
53	//   walks the steps in order, executing each through the same per-opcode logic
54	//   as the ring (CMD_LAUNCH_QMD drains its kernel via the launch sub-FSM — the
55	//   inter-stage barrier; CMD_DCR_WRITE / CMD_CACHE_FLUSH apply inline), then
56	//   retires the one OP_DRAW. The whole VS→setup→bin→FF-config→FS sequence runs
57	//   from one host doorbell with no host round-trip — the "true GPU" draw. The
58	//   descriptor is an indirect command bundle, so the executed sequence is
59	//   byte-identical to streaming the same commands through the ring.
60	// ============================================================================
61	
62	#ifndef VORTEX_COMMAND_PROCESSOR_H
63	#define VORTEX_COMMAND_PROCESSOR_H
64	
65	#include <cstdint>
66	#include <functional>
67	#include <array>
68	#include <vm_types.h>   // SATP_t / PTE_t / vAddr_t (VM page-table walk)
69	
70	namespace vortex {
71	
72	class CommandProcessor {
73	public:
74	    struct Hooks {
75	        // Read `bytes` bytes from device DRAM at `addr` into `dst`.
76	        // Used for ring-buffer fetches (one cache line at a time).
77	        std::function<void(uint64_t addr, void* dst, std::size_t bytes)> dram_read;
78	
79	        // Write `bytes` bytes from `src` into device DRAM at `addr`.
80	        // Used for completion-slot writebacks (8 B seqnum).
81	        std::function<void(uint64_t addr, const void* src, std::size_t bytes)> dram_write;
82	
83	        // Issue a single DCR write to Vortex (for CMD_DCR_WRITE).
84	        std::function<void(uint32_t addr, uint32_t value)> vortex_dcr_write;
85	
86	        // Issue a single DCR read to Vortex (for CMD_DCR_READ). `tag` is
87	        // placed on the DCR data bus and addresses things like per-core
88	        // CACHE_FLUSH. The backend must block until the response is
89	        // available before returning.
90	        std::function<uint32_t(uint32_t addr, uint32_t tag)> vortex_dcr_read;
91	
92	        // Pulse Vortex's start signal (for CMD_LAUNCH). The launch FSM
93	        // calls this once when transitioning into the "started" state.
94	        std::function<void()> vortex_start;
95	
96	        // Query Vortex's busy state. The launch FSM waits for this to
97	        // rise (kernel actually executing) then fall (kernel done)
98	        // before retiring the CMD_LAUNCH.
99	        std::function<bool()> vortex_busy;
100	    };
101	
102	    explicit CommandProcessor(const Hooks& hooks);
103	
104	    // ----- Host-facing MMIO surface -----
105	    // Offsets match VX_cp_axil_regfile (CP-internal, 0-based).
106	    // Backends doing MMIO at byte offset 0x1000+ should subtract 0x1000
107	    // on their side before calling these.
108	    void     mmio_write(uint32_t off, uint32_t value);
109	    uint32_t mmio_read (uint32_t off) const;
110	
111	    // ----- Sim integration -----
112	    // Advance the CP one functional cycle. Called by the simulator's
113	    // per-cycle loop. Cheap: a small FSM step (single-digit branches).
114	    void tick();
115	
116	    // True iff CP_CTRL.enable_global && Q_CONTROL.enable. The simulator
117	    // can use this to skip tick() when the host hasn't enabled the CP.
118	    bool enabled() const;
119	
120	    // True iff the engine has commands in flight OR ring has pending
121	    // entries. Lets the host's wait loop break early when the CP is idle.
122	    bool busy() const;
123	
124	private:
125	    // Engine FSM states. DrawStep / DrawLaunchWait walk an OP_DRAW bundle.
126	    enum class EngState { Idle, Decode, Bid, WaitDone, Retire,
127	                          DrawStep, DrawLaunchWait };
128	
129	    // KMU launch sub-FSM.
130	    enum class LaunchState { Idle, PulseStart, WaitBusy, WaitDrain };
131	
132	    // Command opcodes: low 8 bits of the on-wire command header.
133	    enum : uint8_t {
134	        OP_NOP        = 0x00,
135	        OP_MEM_WRITE  = 0x01,
136	        OP_MEM_READ   = 0x02,
137	        OP_MEM_COPY   = 0x03,
138	        OP_DCR_WRITE  = 0x04,
139	        OP_DCR_READ   = 0x05,
140	        OP_LAUNCH     = 0x06,
141	        OP_FENCE      = 0x07,
142	        OP_EVENT_SIG  = 0x08,
143	        OP_EVENT_WAIT = 0x09,
144	        OP_CACHE_FLUSH = 0x0A,
145	        OP_LAUNCH_QMD = 0x0B,  // atomic launch: KMU descriptor read from memory
146	        OP_DRAW       = 0x0C,  // device-orchestrated draw: arg0 = draw descriptor addr
147	    };
148	
149	    // Fixed per-step stride inside a draw descriptor: the 28-byte cmd-record
150	    // prefix (opcode/flags/reserved + arg0/arg1/arg2). A uniform stride keeps
151	    // the descriptor walk (and the RTL CP mirror) simple.
152	    static constexpr int DRAW_STEP_BYTES = 28;
153	    static constexpr uint32_t MAX_DRAW_STEPS = 256;  // corrupt-count backstop
154	
155	    // CMD_MEM_* header flag (cmd_t.flags bit2 = F_MEM_PHYSICAL): the device
156	    // operand is a physical address — the MMU-aware CP DMA skips translation.
157	    // Used for page-table bootstrap writes and the PT region itself. A
158	    // dedicated bit, distinct from flags bit0 (F_PROFILE) — the addressing
159	    // mode is its own descriptor field (modern-GPU convention).
160	    static constexpr uint8_t MEM_FLAG_PHYSICAL = 0x04;
161	
162	    // Decoded cmd record (matches cmd_t struct layout on-wire).
163	    struct Cmd {
164	        uint8_t  opcode;
165	        uint8_t  flags;
166	        uint16_t reserved;
167	        uint64_t arg0;
168	        uint64_t arg1;
169	        uint64_t arg2;
170	    };
171	
172	    // ----- Per-queue programmable state (q_state_t mirror) -----
173	    struct Queue {
174	        uint64_t ring_base   = 0;
175	        uint64_t head_addr   = 0;
176	        uint64_t cmpl_addr   = 0;
177	        uint8_t  ring_log2   = 16;     // 64 KiB default
178	        uint32_t control     = 0;      // bit0=enable, bits3:2=prio
179	        uint64_t tail        = 0;
180	        uint32_t tail_lo_staging = 0;
181	        // CP-tracked state (not host-writable):
182	        uint64_t head        = 0;      // bytes consumed
183	        uint64_t seqnum      = 0;      // commands retired
184	        uint32_t error       = 0;
185	    };
186	
187	    // ----- Globals -----
188	    uint32_t cp_ctrl_ = 0;           // bit0=enable_global
189	    uint64_t satp_ = 0;              // CP_SATP — page-table root for the CP DMA's MMU
190	    uint64_t cycle_counter_ = 0;
191	    Queue    q0_;                    // single-queue model
192	    Hooks    hooks_;
193	    uint32_t last_dcr_rsp_ = 0;     // Q_LAST_DCR_RSP slot (0x130)
194	
195	    // ----- Engine/launch state machines -----
196	    EngState    eng_state_ = EngState::Idle;
197	    LaunchState launch_state_ = LaunchState::Idle;
198	    Cmd         cur_cmd_{};
199	    bool        cur_is_launch_ = false;
200	    bool        cur_is_no_resource_ = false;
201	
202	    // ----- Draw-bundle state (OP_DRAW walk) -----
203	    uint64_t    draw_phys_      = 0;   // descriptor base (translated)
204	    uint32_t    draw_num_steps_ = 0;
205	    uint32_t    draw_step_      = 0;
206	    Cmd         draw_cmd_{};           // decoded current step
207	
208	    // ----- Fetch state -----
209	    // The simulator fetches one cache line at a time when head < tail,
210	    // then walks the CL extracting decoded cmds before fetching the next.
211	    static constexpr std::size_t CL_BYTES = 64;
212	    static constexpr int MAX_CMDS_PER_CL = 5;
213	    std::array<uint8_t, CL_BYTES> cl_buf_{};
214	    int  cl_cmd_count_ = 0;
215	    int  cl_cmd_slot_ = 0;
216	    bool cl_loaded_   = false;
217	
218	    // Walk `cl_buf_` and populate `decoded_cmds_` / `cl_cmd_count_`.
219	    void unpack_cl();
220	    // Decode a single header at byte offset `off` into a Cmd record;
221	    // returns the size in bytes of the command (so caller can advance).
222	    int  decode_cmd(int off, Cmd& out);
223	    // Decode a cmd record from an arbitrary byte buffer (shared by the ring
224	    // unpacker and the OP_DRAW step walk).
225	    static int decode_cmd_bytes(const uint8_t* buf, int len, int off, Cmd& out);
226	    // Execute one DCR_WRITE / DCR_READ / CACHE_FLUSH / EVENT_SIG / MEM_* /
227	    // LAUNCH_QMD step against `c` (shared by the ring Bid path and OP_DRAW).
228	    // Returns true if a kernel launch was kicked (caller must wait for drain).
229	    bool exec_inline_cmd_(const Cmd& c);
230	    // Read the next OP_DRAW step from the descriptor into draw_cmd_.
231	    void draw_load_step_();
232	    // Inverse of decoded helpers: write seqnum to cmpl_addr.
233	    void publish_completion();
234	    // CMD_EVENT_WAIT compare helper — reads cur_cmd_.arg0 from DRAM and
235	    // compares to cur_cmd_.arg1 under the wait_op encoded in arg2[1:0].
236	    bool event_wait_satisfied_();
237	    // CMD_LAUNCH_QMD: read the in-memory KMU descriptor at `qmd_addr` and
238	    // replay its {dcr_addr,value} pairs through the DCR-write hook.
239	    void apply_qmd_(uint64_t qmd_addr);
240	    // Advance the launch FSM one step using cur_cmd_.
241	    void tick_launch();
242	    // Advance the engine FSM one step.
243	    void tick_engine();
244	    // Fetch one CL from ring into cl_buf_ if needed.
245	    void fetch_if_needed();
246	    // VM: translate a device virtual address to physical via a page-table
247	    // walk. A no-op when VM is disabled, SATP is unset/BARE, or physical.
248	    uint64_t cp_translate(uint64_t vaddr, bool physical) const;
249	};
250	
251	} // namespace vortex

253	#endif // VORTEX_COMMAND_PROCESSOR_H

4	`include "VX_define.vh"
5	
6	// ============================================================================
7	// VX_cp_engine — per-queue Command Processor Engine (CPE).
8	//
9	// Consumes a decoded command stream on `cmd_in`, classifies each command
10	// onto one of three shared resources (KMU / DMA / DCR), bids for the
11	// resource through the engine_bid interface, and retires the command
12	// once the resource signals done.
13	//
14	// FSM:
15	//   IDLE         : no command in hand; assert cmd_in_ready
16	//   DECODE       : combinational classification of cmd opcode -> resource
17	//   BID          : assert bid line for the chosen resource
18	//   WAIT_DONE    : hold bid until resource signals done
19	//   RETIRE       : pulse retire_evt + advance seqnum; back to IDLE
20	//
21	// Opcodes handled:
22	//   - CMD_NOP / CMD_FENCE                          (retire immediately)
23	//   - CMD_LAUNCH                                   (bid KMU)
24	//   - CMD_DCR_WRITE / CMD_DCR_READ / CMD_CACHE_FLUSH (bid DCR)
25	//   - CMD_MEM_*                                    (bid DMA)
26	//   - CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL / CMD_EVENT_WAIT            (bid EVENT)
27	// ============================================================================
28	
29	module VX_cp_engine
30	  import VX_cp_pkg::*;
31	#(
32	  parameter int QID = 0
33	)(
34	  input  wire clk,
35	  input  wire reset,
36	
37	  // Queue priority (a field of the regfile's q_state) used to tag the
38	  // arbiter bids. The engine needs nothing else from the queue state.
39	  input  wire [1:0]               prio_in,
40	  // Retired sequence-number telemetry back to the regfile's Q_SEQNUM.
41	  // A bare scalar (not a cpe_state_t passthrough): see the seqnum_out
42	  // driver below for why.
43	  output wire [63:0]              seqnum_out,
44	
45	  // Decoded command stream input (driven by VX_cp_fetch + VX_cp_unpack).
46	  input  wire                     cmd_in_valid,
47	  input  cmd_t                    cmd_in,
48	  output logic                    cmd_in_ready,
49	
50	  // Bid lines to the four resource arbiters.
51	  VX_cp_engine_bid_if.bidder      bid_kmu,
52	  VX_cp_engine_bid_if.bidder      bid_dma,
53	  VX_cp_engine_bid_if.bidder      bid_dcr,
54	  VX_cp_engine_bid_if.bidder      bid_event,
55	
56	  // Per-resource done signals. These come from the resource module
57	  // (launch/dma/dcr_proxy/event_unit) and pulse high for one cycle when
58	  // the resource finishes the current command. The engine consumes them
59	  // in S_WAIT_DONE to know when to retire.
60	  input  wire                     kmu_done_i,
61	  input  wire                     dma_done_i,
62	  input  wire                     dcr_done_i,
63	  input  wire                     event_done_i,
64	
65	  // Retirement signaling to VX_cp_completion. `retire_evt` is held high in
66	  // S_RETIRE until `retire_ready_i` is observed — valid/ready handshake so
67	  // completion never drops a seqnum on cycle collisions (see
68	  // VX_cp_completion's per-source latch).
69	  output logic                    retire_evt,
70	  output logic [63:0]             retire_seqnum,
71	  input  wire                     retire_ready_i,
72	
73	  // Profiling sample pulses (consumed by the event unit).
74	  output logic                    submit_evt,
75	  output logic                    start_evt,
76	  output logic                    end_evt,
77	  output logic [63:0]             profile_slot
78	);
79	
80	  typedef enum logic [2:0] {
81	    S_IDLE,
82	    S_DECODE,
83	    S_BID,
84	    S_WAIT_DONE,
85	    S_RETIRE
86	  } state_e;
87	
88	  state_e       fsm;
89	  cmd_t         cur_cmd;
90	  cp_resource_e cur_res;
91	  logic         no_resource;        // true for opcodes that bypass arbiters (NOP, FENCE, EVENT_*)
92	  logic [63:0]  seqnum_r;
93	
94	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
95	  // Opcode → resource classification (combinational over cur_cmd).
96	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
97	  function automatic cp_resource_e classify(cp_opcode_e op,
98	                                            output logic skip);
99	    skip = 1'b0;
100	    case (op)
101	      CMD_LAUNCH:                    return RES_KMU;
102	      CMD_DCR_WRITE, CMD_DCR_READ,
103	      CMD_CACHE_FLUSH:               return RES_DCR;
104	      CMD_MEM_WRITE,
105	      CMD_MEM_READ,
106	      CMD_MEM_COPY:                  return RES_DMA;
107	      CMD_EVENT_SIGNAL,
108	      CMD_EVENT_WAIT:                return RES_EVT;
109	      default: begin
110	        skip = 1'b1;
111	        return RES_KMU;   // unused when skip=1
112	      end
113	    endcase
114	  endfunction
115	
116	  // The done pulses (kmu_done_i / dma_done_i / dcr_done_i) are broadcast
117	  // from the shared resource modules to every CPE. The bid arbiter grants
118	  // one CPE per resource at a time and the resource processes one command
119	  // at a time, so only the granted CPE is in S_WAIT_DONE when the matching
120	  // pulse arrives; non-granted CPEs ignore it.
121	
122	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
123	  // FSM
124	  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	
126	  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
127	    automatic cp_resource_e res;
128	    automatic logic         skip_flag;
129	    if (reset) begin
130	      fsm         <= S_IDLE;
131	      cur_cmd     <= '0;
132	      cur_res     <= RES_KMU;
133	      no_resource <= 1'b0;
134	      seqnum_r    <= '0;

# 命令处理器与 KMU

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲把前面几讲里反复出现的「主机写一组 DCR、然后启动内核」这件事，从黑盒彻底打开。读完本讲，你应当能够：

- 说清 **命令处理器（Command Processor，CP）** 的整体结构：AXI-Lite 寄存器接口、主机驻留命令环（command ring）、命令格式，以及它把每条命令分流到「KMU / DMA / DCR / EVENT」四个共享资源的机制。
- 画出每队列引擎（CPE）的状态机 `IDLE→DECODE→BID→WAIT_DONE→RETIRE`，并解释完成号（seqnum）如何安全地回写主机。
- 解释 **KMU（Kernel Management Unit，内核管理单元）** 如何从一次 `CMD_LAUNCH` 进展到「脉冲 start → 等 busy 拉高 → 等 busy 拉低（drain）」的完整生命周期。
- 看懂 KMU 如何根据 `grid/block/cluster` 维度把一个网格遍历成一串 CTA 请求，并理解 `cta_id`、`block_idx`、`is_first_of_cluster` 这些字段的来源。
- 对照 RTL CP（`hw/rtl/cp/`）与仿真 CP（`sim/common/cmd_processor.cpp`）两套实现，知道它们的对应关系与当前已知的分歧点（VM、QMD launch 等）。

本讲承接 u3-l4（主机如何加载 `.vxbin` 并写 KMU DCR）与 u6-l1（CTA 如何被拆成 warp），把二者之间那条「命令处理器 → KMU → CTA」的控制链路补齐。

## 2. 前置知识

在进入源码前，先建立三个直觉。

**（1）主机从不直接写设备内存，也从不直接启动核。** 回顾 u3-l2：主机与设备之间唯一的控制通路是 **CP（命令处理器）**，唯一的搬运工是 **CP 的 DMA 引擎**。主机做的事只有两类：往 CP 的 AXI-Lite 寄存器里写控制字、往「CP 可见的主机内存」里写命令环。真正去戳设备 DCR、去搬数据、去拉起内核的，是 CP 自己。所以「启动一次内核」本质上是「主机往环里写一串命令，再敲一下门铃（doorbell）」。

**（2）命令环在主机内存里，不在设备里。** 这是一个工程取舍：环放在主机 pin 住的内存里，CP 通过它独占的 `axi_host` 端口去取（一次取一个 64 字节 cache line）。这样做的好处是主机追加命令就是普通的 `memcpy`，不需要每条命令都做一次 MMIO；坏处是 CP 必须有读主机内存的能力。这条决策记录在设计文档里（见 [command_processor.md:427-432](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/docs/designs/command_processor.md#L427-L432)，明确说「设备内存环 + 每命令 DMA」的旧方案被废弃）。

**（3）CTA 是 GPU 的调度单位。** 一个 CTA（Cooperative Thread Array，对应 CUDA 的 thread block）是一组会共享本地内存（LMEM）和屏障的线程。主机用 `grid_dim × block_dim` 描述一次 launch：`block_dim` 是一个 CTA 内的线程数，`grid_dim` 是 CTA 的个数。KMU 的职责就是把 `grid` 这个三维计数空间**展开成一串 CTA 请求**，每个 CTA 带着自己的 `block_idx`。注意本讲里的 **cluster**（`cluster_dim`）是 **CTA 簇**——一组协作的 CTA，用于 DXA 多播与跨 CTA 屏障（参见 u9-l2），**不要**和 u7-l1/u8-l1 里「cluster 共享 L2」的内存层次 cluster 混淆，两者同名但含义不同。

| 术语 | 全称 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| CP | Command Processor | 设备侧命令处理器，唯一控制通路 |
| CPE | CP Engine | 每队列一个的命令引擎 |
| KMU | Kernel Management Unit | 内核管理单元，展开 grid 为 CTA |
| CTA | Cooperative Thread Array | 线程块，GPU 调度单位 |
| DCR | Device Control Register | 设备控制寄存器 |
| doorbell | — | 主机写 `Q_TAIL` 通知 CP「有新命令了」 |
| seqnum | sequence number | 每条命令退休时递增的完成号 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CP 顶层架构与命令格式

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

CP 是 Vortex 的**单一控制平面**：主机提交给 GPU 的所有工作——内存搬运、DCR 编程、内核启动、栅栏、事件、缓存维护——都走这一条路。在 FPGA 目标（XRT / OPAE）上它甚至是**唯一**的 launch/DCR 通路，旧的 AP_CTRL 启动状态机已被移除（见 [command_processor.md:17-21](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/docs/designs/command_processor.md#L17-L21)）。

CP 的设计可以用一句话概括：**N 个并行命令引擎（每队列一个），喂给 4 个轮转仲裁器，仲裁器串行化对 4 个共享资源的访问**——内核管理单元（KMU 启动）、DMA 引擎、DCR 总线、事件单元。命令环在主机内存里；CP 用独占的 AXI 主端口去取环、去写完成号。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

主机侧一次「提交命令」的全流程：

1. 运行时的每队列 worker 线程把若干命令编码进**一个 64 字节 cache line**，`memcpy` 进主机驻留的环缓冲。
2. 主机写 `Q_TAIL_LO` 暂存、写 `Q_TAIL_HI` **原子提交**（doorbell）。
3. CP 的 `VX_cp_fetch` 发现 `head < tail`，通过 `axi_host` 取回一个 64B line。
4. `VX_cp_unpack` 按 opcode 的字节长度逐条解出 `cmd_t`。
5. 该队列的 `VX_cp_engine` 把每条命令分类到一个资源，向对应仲裁器竞标（bid）。
6. 仲裁器轮转授权一个引擎，资源单元执行命令。
7. 命令完成后，`VX_cp_completion` 把 8 字节 seqnum 写回主机驻留的 `cmpl_addr`，seqnum 递增。
8. 主机 busy-poll `Q_SEQNUM`，看到它前进就知道命令已完成。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**顶层 `VX_cp_core`** 把所有零件拼起来。它的端口里最关键的是两个 AXI 主端口——`axi_host`（到主机内存）和 `axi_dev`（到设备内存），以及一个 AXI-Lite 从端口（到主机的 MMIO 寄存器）：

- 顶层模块声明与双 AXI 端口：[VX_cp_core.sv:77-98](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L77-L98)——说明 CP 对外就这三条路：一条_lite 接收主机寄存器写、两条 AXI 取环/搬数据。
- 唯一的 AXI-Lite 从模块 `VX_cp_axil_regfile`：[VX_cp_core.sv:135](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L135)——全局寄存器 + 每队列块都在这里，doorbell 在 `Q_TAIL_HI` 写时原子提交。
- 每队列一对 `VX_cp_fetch` + `VX_cp_engine`：[VX_cp_core.sv:186-197](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L186-L197)。
- 四个资源各一个轮转仲裁器：[VX_cp_core.sv:276-291](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L276-L291)。
- 双 AXI xbar：host xbar（fetch+completion+DMA(host)→`axi_host`）在 [VX_cp_core.sv:389](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L389)，device xbar（DMA(dev)+event→`axi_dev`）在 [VX_cp_core.sv:440](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_core.sv#L440)。

**命令格式**定义在 `VX_cp_pkg.sv`。一条命令 = 4 字节头 + opcode 特定载荷，打包进 64 字节 cache line（每行最多 5 条，零头终止本行）：

- opcode 枚举：[VX_cp_pkg.sv:63-75](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L63-L75)——`CMD_LAUNCH = 0x06` 是本讲主角。
- 4 字节头 `{reserved[16], flags[8], opcode[8]}`：[VX_cp_pkg.sv:84-88](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L84-L88)。
- 解码后的命令记录 `cmd_t`（头 + 三个 64 位 arg + 可选 profile 槽）：[VX_cp_pkg.sv:97-103](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L97-L103)。
- 每个 opcode 的在线字节长度表：[VX_cp_pkg.sv:183-201](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/hw/rtl/cp/VX_cp_pkg.sv#L183-L201)——注意 `CMD_LAUNCH` 只有 12 字节（头 + 一个 8B arg），这是它「轻量脉冲」性质的体现：真正的内核参数已经通过前面的 `CMD_DCR_WRITE` 写进 KMU 寄存器了，`CMD_LAUNCH` 只负责「点火」。

> **为何 launch 只有 12 字节？** 因为当前架构下，一次 launch 被编码成「约 18 条 `CMD_DCR_WRITE`（写满 KMU 的 STARTUP_ADDR/KERNEL_ENTRY/ARG/grid/block/cluster 等 DCR）+ 1 条 `CMD_LAUNCH`」。`CMD_LAUNCH` 自身不带参数，只是脉冲。设计文档把「用一条带内联参数的原子 `CMD_LAUNCH_QMD` 替代这 18 条 DCR 写」列为未来改进（见 4.5 节与 [command_processor.md:397-400](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/docs/designs/command_processor.md#L397-L400)）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么命令环要放在主机内存而不是设备内存？如果放在设备内存，主机追加命令的开销会变成什么？

> **参考答案**：环放主机内存时，主机追加命令是一次普通 `memcpy`，零 MMIO；CP 用 `axi_host` 主动取。若放设备内存，主机每追加一条命令都要做一次 MMIO/DMA 写设备，开销高且 CP 仍要一段设备可见缓冲。设计文档明确废弃了「设备内存环 + 每命令 DMA」的旧方案（[command_processor.md:428-429](https://github.com/vortexgpgpu/vortex/blob/d76b7f24e658867ab57e3942d7c648c3e6af072d/docs/designs/command_processor.md#L428-L429)）。

**练习 2**：一条 64 字节的 cache line 最多能装几条 `CMD_LAUNCH`？装几条 `CMD_MEM_WRITE`？

> **参考答案**：`CMD_LAUNCH` = 12 字节，\( \lfloor 64/12 \rfloor = 5 \) 条，正好是 `MAX_CMDS_PER_CL`；`CMD_MEM_WRITE` = 28 字节，\( \lfloor 64/28 \rfloor = 2 \) 条（剩余 8 字节放不下第三条，会被零头终止或填 NOP）。
